_about: The world calendar: twelve 30-day months of three tendays, five holy days between months, and a leap day every fourth year. Festivals are dated by month and day; 'days' is how long one lasts and 'every' repeats it inside that span. 'where' is "Everywhere" or a list of place titles. Approved by Austin (2026-10-20).

holyDays.name: Hearthnight
holyDays.text: Midwinter. Families gather at the fire, every Hearth temple opens as a refuge, and no door may be shut on a traveller.

holyDays.name: First Furrow
holyDays.by: Church of the Hearth, Church of the Earth
holyDays.text: Hearth and Earth priests bless the fields and the first ploughing. Weddings held today are lucky.

holyDays.name: Midsummer
holyDays.text: The Day of Heroes. The Church of the Hero names the year's honoured champions, and at the Salt Mirror the reflection and the sky change places for an hour.

holyDays.name: The Pressing
holyDays.text: The Revels' harvest and wine festival, the biggest feast of the year in most of the realm.

holyDays.name: Night of Names
holyDays.text: The Church of Death reads aloud the names of the year's dead, and every town reads the names it lost to monster surges.

leapDay.name: Concord Day
leapDay.by: Church of Trade, Church of Justice
leapDay.text: Trade and Justice witness the renewal of treaties, charters and long contracts. Oaths sworn today are said to bind twice as hard.

events.name: New Year's Reckoning
events.text: Debts fall due, ledgers close and guild fees are paid. Moneylenders are busy and tempers short.

events.name: Stormcall
events.by: Church of the Storm, Church of the Ocean
events.text: Sailors pray for a kind season before the shipping lanes reopen. Bad omens keep ships in harbour.

events.name: Roadopening
events.text: Caravans are blessed at the gates and pilgrims set out on their year-and-a-day walk. Escort contracts are everywhere.

events.name: Mending Day
events.text: Healing at the temples is free from dawn to dusk, and the queues are long.

events.name: Crown Day
events.text: Oaths of fealty are renewed and new titles granted. Petitioners flood the court.

events.name: Chainbreaking
events.text: Debtors and bonded servants may be bought free. Followers of Liberty and Dominion often clash in the street.

events.name: Society Trials
events.text: New adventurers are licensed and rank assessments are held in public. Teams recruit.

events.name: Convocation
events.text: Open demonstrations of new magic and new astral finds. Rivals sabotage each other.

events.name: Blessing of the Waters
events.text: Fleets and river barges are blessed, and offerings are thrown into the water.

events.name: The Great Fair
events.text: A tenday market with merchants from far away. Rare goods appear and prices drop.

events.name: Masked ball
events.text: One of the season's masked balls. Perfect for intrigue, disguises and assassinations.

events.name: Flower Wine Festival
events.text: The event of Vitesse's year, held on the river terraces. The great houses all attend.

events.name: Sheaf Day
events.text: The first sheaf of the harvest is cut and carried to the Hearth shrine, and the first loaf from it is shared by the whole village.

events.name: Orchard Fair
events.by: Church of Trade, Church of the Revels
events.text: Three days of fruit, cider and pie-judging on the farmland around Vitesse. Buyers come from every city to bid on the crop.

events.name: Scarecrow Judging
events.text: Scarecrows dressed as famous adventurers are judged, far too seriously.

events.name: Lamplighting
events.by: Church of Knowledge, Church of Truth
events.text: Libraries and archives open to all for a day, and old secrets sometimes come out.

events.name: Reedharvest
events.by: Church of the Ocean, harvest custom
events.text: The delta's reed and rice harvest. Boats are hung with lanterns and the flats are lit all night.

events.name: Granary Sealing
events.text: Granaries are sealed for the winter, and offerings are buried at the edge of every field. A short count now means a hungry winter.

events.name: Night of Masks
events.by: Church of Disguise, Church of the Revels
events.text: Everyone goes masked from dusk to dawn, and nothing done in a mask is spoken of.

events.name: Hunters' Feast
events.by: Church of the Hero, harvest custom
events.text: The last harvest of the year: game and monster meat. Hunters and adventurers sell their kills, and the biggest trophy wins a cask.

events.name: The Muster
events.text: Garrisons and house guards parade, and the year's recruits swear in. Duels are fought.

events.name: The Longest Night
events.text: Bonfires burn the old year's things, and Purity preachers hunt for corruption.
